ElementDescription: Although Marcus knows how to speak properly, he often talks baby talk when he's at home. His mother finds this very annoying. In order to reduce this behavior, she should:
Notes: 1 = Ignore his baby talk and talk to him when he makes sense; 2 = Scold his baby talk and tell him to act his age; 3 = Try to understand his baby talk, translate it into grown-up or normal talk, and encourage him to imitate the correct response

ElementDescription: Whenever Lisas father sits down to help her with her homework, Lisa often looks away, leaves her chair, and walks around the room. She does this most during the first minute or two. Her father should:
Notes: 1 = Offer her a large reward for doing her homework; 2 = Reward her for sitting quietly and looking at the homework; 3 = Try to hold her interest by talking about what she's done in school

ElementDescription: Kim has learned that she is sent to her room for five minutes every time she ignores her grandmothers requests. When would it be OK to give her a second chance?
Notes: 1 = If she promises not to do it again; 2 = If Kim says she didn't hear her grandmother; 3 = Neither of these

ElementDescription: Paul often tries to get his sisters attention by slapping her. When his sister ignores him, he often hits her harder or kicks her. To stop this behavior, Paul's mother should:
Notes: 1 = Put Paul in time out for five minutes. If he hits his sister again, put him in timeout for another five minutes; 2 = Put him in time out until he calms down; 3 = Hit Paul back

ElementDescription: The guidance counselor has told Jonathans mother that he is aggressive. The first step to changing this aggression is to:
Notes: 1 = Ask Jonathan why he is aggressive; 2 = Teach Jonathan to express his aggression more appropriately; 3 = Ask the guidance counselor to specify what behaviors led her to call Jonathan aggressive

ElementDescription: Cynthias grandmother wishes that she had more time to spend with her granddaughter, who seems to be ''starved for attention.''  She should:
Notes: 1 = Set aside one Saturday every month to spend the day with her at the park; 2 = Explain to her that her grandmother works hard and cannot play with her all the time; 3 = Spend 5 minutes every day playing with her

ElementDescription: Brandon got angry when his father told him that it was time to clean up his crayons and so he broke them all. To teach Brandon a lesson, his father should:
Notes: 1 = Send him to his room for fifteen minutes; 2 = Make him clean up the mess and tell him that because he broke his crayons, he will have to color with broken crayons; 3 = Buy him new crayons and tell him that if he breaks them, he will not get anymore

ElementDescription: Five year-old Tonys mother wants him to put his dirty plate in the sink after dinner. The best way to tell him is by saying:
Notes: 1 = Tony, put your dirty dish in the sink; 2 = Don't leave a mess, Tony; 3 = Let's all clean up!

ElementDescription: Every morning, 6-year-old Kyra's mother expects her to put on her clothes, brush her teeth, and come to the breakfast table. So that Kyra does not forget her morning routine, her mother should:
Notes: 1 = Give her many reminders the night before and when she first wakes up; 2 = Scold her if she forgets to do these things; 3 = Sit down with Kyra and make a list of the things she needs to do in the morning and then post it in her bedroom

ElementDescription: A mother notices that she has been snapping at her children because she is stressed out with all of her parenting responsibilities. She should:
Notes: 1 = Make time to do something enjoyable without the children so that she can re-energize; 2 = Explain to the children that they should behave because she is stressed out; 3 = Try to spend as much time as possible in her own room and away from the children so that she will not snap at them
